before: Every local undo entry in TreeDocumentStore held the whole package as it was, including its own copy of the body's child list.
after: An entry below the top of its stack keeps wide elements as chunks shared with neighbouring entries. Undo and redo rebuild the same content: equal package, part and root objects, and the same block objects.
reason: Local undo history is not shared state. The operation encoding, node ids, snapshots, and awareness payloads do not change, and the id allocator keeps its lineage across a rebuilt root, so ids stay monotone. Remote edits still apply through the same transactions.
